segments.text: So today's topic is electrical safety rules that every worker needs to know.

segments.text: So the first rule of electrical safety is that you always have to assume that the electrical wire you see on the side is in live condition.
segments.zh: 用电安全的第一条规则是，你要始终假定你在现场看到的电线是带电的。

segments.text: You never have to assume that the electrical wire you see on the side is in live condition.
segments.zh: 你绝不能假定你在现场看到的电线是带电的。

segments.text: You have to assume that the electrical wire you see on the side is in live condition.
segments.zh: 你要假定你在现场看到的电线是带电的。

segments.text: Whenever you work on an electrical circuit or equipment, you have to treat it before working on it.
segments.zh: 每当你在电路或设备上作业时，在作业之前你都要这样对待它：

segments.text: The electrical circuit or equipment panel that you see on the side is energized.
segments.zh: 你在现场看到的电路或设备配电盘是带电的，

segments.text: You have to consider it.
segments.zh: 你要这样认为，

segments.text: You have to believe that it is not powered off.
segments.zh: 你要相信它并没有断电，

segments.text: Although it has been powered off.
segments.zh: 尽管它已经断电了。

segments.text: But here you have to verify it by using the voltage tester you have.
segments.zh: 但在这里你要用你手上的验电器来核实，

segments.text: You have to verify it cross-verify that it is powered off or it is powered off.
segments.zh: 你要核实、交叉核实它是否已经断电。

segments.text: Because many accidents have been seen that it has been caused by miscommunications or faulty disconnections.
segments.zh: 因为已经发现很多事故是由于沟通失误或断电不当造成的。

segments.text: So you have to assume that the electrical wire you see on the side is in live condition.
segments.zh: 所以你要假定你在现场看到的电线是带电的。

segments.text: This is the first rule of electrical that every worker needs to know.
segments.zh: 这就是每个工人都需要知道的第一条用电规则。

segments.text: The second rule of electrical is the lock out and tag out procedures.
segments.zh: 第二条用电规则是上锁挂牌程序，

segments.text: You have to use this.
segments.zh: 你要使用它。

segments.text: Because lotto ensures that the electrical system has been properly shut off.
segments.zh: 因为上锁挂牌能确保电气系统已被正确断开，

segments.text: And now the electrical system has been shut off properly.
segments.zh: 而现在电气系统已被正确断开，

segments.text: Now it cannot be re-energized again until your maintenance or repair is going on.
segments.zh: 在你的维护或维修进行期间，它就不会被重新通电。

segments.text: The third rule of electrical safety is that you have to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment.
segments.zh: 第三条用电安全规则是，你要穿戴合适的个人防护装备。

segments.text: Now if you are working as an electrical worker,
segments.zh: 如果你是一名电气作业人员，

segments.text: then make sure that you wear insulated gloves, flame resistance clothing, safety goggles,
segments.zh: 那么每当你操作电气系统时，一定要戴绝缘手套、穿阻燃服、戴安全护目镜，

segments.text: or non-conductive footwear whenever you handle the electrical system.
segments.zh: 或者穿不导电的鞋。

segments.text: The next safety rule is that you have to keep a safe distance from the live electrical lines.
segments.zh: 下一条安全规则是，你要与带电的电线保持安全距离。

segments.text: Now see how much you should keep a safe distance from the live electrical lines.
segments.zh: 现在来看看你应该与带电的电线保持多大的安全距离，

segments.text: This is also very important.
segments.zh: 这也非常重要，

segments.text: Because if there is a high voltage line, then it is possible that you will get an electric shock.
segments.zh: 因为如果是高压线，你就有可能触电。

segments.text: So it is very important that you have to keep a proper clearance from the overhead or underground power lines.
segments.zh: 所以非常重要的是，你要与架空或地下电力线保持适当的间距。

segments.text: Now Osha has told us about the specific distance that you should maintain at which voltage level.
segments.zh: OSHA 已经告诉了我们，在什么电压等级下应该保持多大的具体距离。

segments.text: Now especially if there is a line up to 50 KV, then you have to maintain a safe distance of 10 feet.
segments.zh: 特别是如果线路在 50 KV 以下，你就要保持 10 英尺的安全距离。

segments.text: But if there is a line above 50 KV, then you have to maintain a safe distance of 10 feet plus 0.4 inches per KV.
segments.zh: 但如果线路在 50 KV 以上，你就要保持 10 英尺再加上每 KV 0.4 英寸的安全距离。

segments.text: The next safety rule is that you have to use insulated tools for electrical work.
segments.zh: 下一条安全规则是，电气作业要使用绝缘工具。

segments.text: Now always make sure that the handle should be insulated whenever you work on the live circuit.
segments.zh: 每当你在带电电路上作业时，一定要确保手柄是绝缘的。

segments.text: So as an example, I would like to tell you that if you are using screwdrivers, then make sure that the rubber coated handle is there.
segments.zh: 举个例子，如果你使用螺丝刀，一定要确保有橡胶包覆的手柄。

segments.text: Also if you are using plaques, then the insulated should be gripped there.
segments.zh: 另外，如果你使用钳子，那里应该有绝缘的握把，

segments.text: You have to make sure that.
segments.zh: 你要确保这一点。

segments.text: The next safety rule is that you never have to work in weight conditions.
segments.zh: 下一条安全规则是，你绝不能在潮湿条件下作业。

segments.text: Now there can be many types of weight conditions like slippery surface or weight tools.
segments.zh: 潮湿条件可能有很多种，比如湿滑的表面或潮湿的工具。

segments.text: If you are using it, then any slippery surface can be there.
segments.zh: 如果你在使用它，那里就可能会有湿滑的表面。

segments.text: Now why do we say that water should never work on the weight condition?
segments.zh: 那为什么我们说绝不能在潮湿条件下作业呢？

segments.text: Now especially we are talking about electrical here.
segments.zh: 特别是我们这里讲的是用电。

segments.text: So what does water do?

segments.text: Electricity is a good conductor here.

segments.text: Water is a good conductor for electricity.

segments.text: So when you are working on electrical in weight conditions, then you get a lot of electric shock here.
segments.zh: 所以当你在潮湿条件下进行电气作业时，你在这里就很容易触电。

segments.text: So you have to avoid such conditions.
segments.zh: 所以你要避免这样的条件，

segments.text: You don't have to work in any work.
segments.zh: 你不能在任何作业中这样做，

segments.text: Especially in the weight environment, you don't have to work on electricity.
segments.zh: 特别是在潮湿的环境中，你不能进行电气作业。

segments.text: If there is an emergency, then you have to make sure that you have the equipment available.
segments.zh: 如果有紧急情况，你就要确保你有可用的设备，

segments.text: It should be a high rated equipment that is designed for this condition.

segments.text: That's why you have to work.

segments.text: Otherwise you don't have to work in the weight conditions.

segments.text: The next rule of electrical is that you have to avoid the overloading circuit.
segments.zh: 下一条用电规则是，你要避免电路过载。

segments.text: Now there are many types of circuits.
segments.zh: 电路有很多种，

segments.text: What happens there is that you can connect a connection or two connections, three connections, four connections.
segments.zh: 那里的情况是，你可以接一个、两个、三个、四个连接，

segments.text: But if you plug in many devices in a single outlet, then what will happen?
segments.zh: 但如果你在一个插座上插了很多设备，会发生什么呢？

segments.text: It will get overheated.
segments.zh: 它会过热，

segments.text: After it gets overheated, then you have to face the fire or equipment failure.
segments.zh: 过热之后，你就要面对火灾或设备故障。

segments.text: That's why you don't have to overload the circuit.
segments.zh: 所以你不能让电路过载，

segments.text: You have to avoid that.

segments.text: The next electrical rule is that you have to inspect the electrical cords or equipment on a regular basis.
segments.zh: 下一条用电规则是，你要定期检查电线或设备。

segments.text: For example, there are fry wires, damaged insulations or exposed conductors.
segments.zh: 比如有磨损的电线、损坏的绝缘层或外露的导体，

segments.text: That's why you can get a serious shock or face the fire hazard.
segments.zh: 因此你可能受到严重的电击或面临火灾危害。

segments.text: Whenever you see that you have to inspect the cords on a regular basis like daily basis, weekly basis or monthly basis,

segments.text: you have to inspect the electrical cords on your side or equipment on a regular basis.
segments.zh: 你都要定期检查你现场的电线或设备。

segments.text: The next safety rule of electrical is that you have to follow proper grounding practices.
segments.zh: 下一条用电安全规则是，你要遵守正确的接地做法。

segments.text: Proper grounding practices means that whatever you are grounding.

segments.text: And it is very helpful to prevent shock or equipment damage.
